note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: BOOD pipeline: motivation, boundary-feature identification, perturbation, generation, and resulting gains

nodes.name: Manual OOD data is costly
nodes.description: Manually preparing OOD training data incurs substantial human and time costs, and some OOD data distributed outside the ID boundary cannot be collected in the real world.

nodes.name: Automated OOD generation is needed
nodes.description: Automated pipelines that generate OOD data are therefore needed to reduce labor when creating auxiliary outlier datasets.

nodes.name: DreamOOD lacks boundary guarantee
nodes.description: DreamOOD samples from low-likelihood regions of a text-conditioned latent space, but with no explicit relation between low-likelihood regions and decision boundaries it cannot guarantee generated images lie on decision boundaries.

nodes.name: Boundary images are informative
nodes.description: Outliers generated near ID decision boundaries are informative and help the classifier refine its boundary between ID and OOD data.

nodes.name: Text-conditioned latent space
nodes.description: BOOD trains an image encoder with a class-embedding alignment loss against CLIP text embeddings of class names, producing a text-conditioned latent space compatible with the diffusion model input space.

nodes.name: Boundary distance via perturbation steps
nodes.description: The minimum number k of gradient-ascent (sign-gradient, step size alpha) perturbation steps needed to change the classifier's prediction serves as a proxy for an ID feature's distance to the decision boundary, d(z,y)=k bounded by K.

nodes.name: Select ID boundary features
nodes.description: BOOD selects as ID boundary features those whose distances lie in the smallest r% of the distance set.

nodes.name: Synthesize OOD features
nodes.description: Selected boundary features are perturbed along the gradient ascent direction until the prediction switches, then for c additional steps, to yield OOD features around the decision boundary.

nodes.name: Diffusion decodes OOD features to images
nodes.description: The synthesized OOD embedding replaces the class token embedding in the text prompt of a diffusion model to generate pixel-space OOD images.

nodes.name: OOD regularization loss
nodes.description: The OOD detector is regularized with a binary logistic loss that treats ID samples as positive and synthesized OOD images as negative.

nodes.name: State-of-the-art on CIFAR-100
nodes.description: On CIFAR-100, BOOD lowers average FPR95 from 40.31% to 10.67% (29.64% decrease) and raises average AUROC from 90.15% to 97.42% (7.27% improvement) over DreamOOD.

nodes.name: State-of-the-art on ImageNet-100
nodes.description: BOOD also surpasses prior state-of-the-art methods on the ImageNet-100 benchmark.

nodes.name: Both modules are necessary
nodes.description: Ablation shows both boundary-feature identification and OOD feature perturbation are essential: decoding selected ID features directly, or perturbing randomly chosen features, performs worse than full BOOD.

isolated_nodes.name: Dataset setup
isolated_nodes.description: Following DreamOOD, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 are the ID datasets, with SVHN, Places365, Textures, LSUN and iSUN as OOD test sets for CIFAR-100.

isolated_nodes.name: Best c is 2
isolated_nodes.description: Varying post-crossing steps c in {0..5}, c=2 performs best; large c pushes features back into the ID region and small c leaves them too close to the ID boundary.

isolated_nodes.name: Moderate pruning rate r best
isolated_nodes.description: Varying r in {2.5,5,10,20}, a moderate r performs best: small r limits diversity, large r selects features far from the boundary.

isolated_nodes.name: Step size alpha 0.015
isolated_nodes.description: Smaller step size alpha allows finer differentiation of boundary distances; alpha=0.015 is used.

isolated_nodes.name: Comparable compute to DreamOOD
isolated_nodes.description: BOOD's total cost is about 16.72h versus about 16.66h for DreamOOD, dominated by image generation (7.5h) and detector regularization (8.5h).

isolated_nodes.name: Limitations
isolated_nodes.description: BOOD depends on the diffusion model's capability on datasets with large domain discrepancy, classification errors on unseen outlier features can misjudge boundary crossing, and hyperparameters are hard to tune.

structural_reasoning: Argument flows from the cost of OOD data and DreamOOD's weakness to the boundary-based pipeline, then to benchmark gains and ablations. Hyperparameter and cost analyses are isolated.
